reviews.reasoning: Re-derived from both witnesses. Psalm 75 carries rule 'shift' with k=1 in web_mt_offset_map.json, so web:Ps.75.0 = oshb:Ps.75.1, web:Ps.75.1 = oshb:Ps.75.2 and web:Ps.75.2 = oshb:Ps.75.3; the row's 3 refs are arithmetically correct and the title pseudo-ref is the owner-ruled form. oshb:Ps.75.1 is the counted superscription in full, and the 5 labels the row names are present in its bytes, 5 of 5: לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ / אַל תַּשְׁחֵ֑ת / מִזְמ֖וֹר / לְאָסָ֣ף / שִֽׁיר (byte tier). The opener the row names is verse-initial at oshb:Ps.75.2, token 1 of 8 (ה֘וֹדִ֤ינוּ), and collates at byte tier. The seam warrant re-derives independently: oshb:Ps.75.2 carries 1cp ה֘וֹדִ֤ינוּ and ה֭וֹדִינוּ plus 3cp סִ֝פְּר֗וּ, with 0 independent personal pronouns among its 8 tokens, while oshb:Ps.75.3 carries 1cs אֶקַּ֣ח and אֶשְׁפֹּֽט with the independent 1cs pronoun אֲ֝נִ֗י. WEB agrees: “We give thanks to you, God. We give thanks,” (web:Ps.75.1) against “When I choose the appointed time, I will judge blamelessly.” (web:Ps.75.2). A skeleton-tier sweep of the le-Asaph token returns 12 verses book-wide, 11 of them in psalms 73-83, so 'continues the Asaph collection (73-83) inside Book III' is accurate; psalms 72, 73 and 74 all carry rule 'identity', so 'the three identity psalms preceding it' is accurate. Selah: the MT-keyed inventory lists 0 selah verses in psalm 75 other than oshb:Ps.75.4, which lies outside this span, and the row makes 0 selah claims. A 1-verse strophe is unusual, but the person shift at the rear seam is a genuine tier-1 signal and 'medium' confidence is calibrated to it. Two observations, neither a defect: the rejected_alternative sets its two grammatical-person glosses in curly double quotes, which the book-wide convention reserves for WEB text (both fall under check_web_quotes' 2-word floor, so they pass unflagged); and 'in this part' is delivery-partition wording rather than the verse-anchored form the register rules prefer.

All 6 Hebrew runs in this row collate at byte tier against the refs cited beside them, and all 5 dual-cites are arithmetically correct under rule 'shift' k=1. The selah disclosure re-derives exactly: the MT-keyed inventory lists oshb:Ps.75.4 as the only selah verse in psalms 72-75, WEB verse totals for psalms 72, 73, 74 and 75 are 20 + 28 + 23 + 10 = 81, and the inventory carries 71 selah verses and 71 occurrences book-wide — the row's figures of 1, 81 and 71 all hold, the unit is named, and the selah sits interior to the span so it is doing no seam work. The span itself is sound: oshb:Ps.75.3-Ps.75.6 is a continuous 1cs/2mp speech block and oshb:Ps.75.7 drops to 3ms reference. What fails is how two of the row's warrants are stated. Observation: the '81 verses' scope is a delivery-partition scope the row never defines in text-anchored terms, so a reader of the chunk map cannot reconstruct what was swept.

challenges.claim: The rationale states that the strophe's opening verse begins on the emphatic 1cs pronoun, but that pronoun is not verse-initial at oshb:Ps.75.3 — the verse opens on a different word and the pronoun stands mid-verse.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.75.3 = web:Ps.75.2 (psalm 75 rule 'shift', k=1: WEB v + 1 = MT v). Token sequence spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, 6 tokens, byte tier: [1] כִּ֭י [2] אֶקַּ֣ח [3] מוֹעֵ֑ד [4] אֲ֝נִ֗י [5] מֵישָׁרִ֥ים [6] אֶשְׁפֹּֽט. The pronoun the row names is token 4 of 6; token 1 is the particle כִּ֭י. WEB preserves the same order, putting the temporal clause first: “When I choose the appointed time, I will judge blamelessly.” (web:Ps.75.2). The row-set applies the same 'opens on' idiom to genuinely verse-initial material one row later, where oshb:Ps.75.7 does open כִּ֤י לֹ֣א (tokens 1-2, byte tier), so the idiom is being used as a position claim. The 1cs oracle voice at oshb:Ps.75.3 is real (אֶקַּ֣ח, אֶשְׁפֹּֽט, plus the pronoun) and the front seam survives; the positional assertion does not.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative's stated mechanism runs backwards: the quotative at oshb:Ps.75.5 governs the speech that follows it, so it cannot retroactively mark web:Ps.75.2-Ps.75.3 as reported speech addressed to the arrogant and wicked.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.75.5 = web:Ps.75.4. Token sequence spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, 8 tokens, byte tier: [1] אָמַ֣רְתִּי [2] לַֽ֭הוֹלְלִים [3] אַל [4] תָּהֹ֑לּוּ ... — the 1cs qatal is verse-initial, its addressee follows it immediately, and the prohibitive speech follows the addressee. Both witnesses delimit the quoted speech to what stands after the frame: WEB opens its inner quotation immediately after “I said to the arrogant,” (web:Ps.75.4) and closes it at the close of “speak with a stiff neck.” (web:Ps.75.5). Neither witness places web:Ps.75.2-Ps.75.3 (= oshb:Ps.75.3-Ps.75.4) inside that speech or directs those verses at the arrogant and wicked; oshb:Ps.75.4 addresses no one and states a 1cs act on the earth's pillars. The divine-oracle reading the row defends is defensible on other grounds — the 1cs claims to set מוֹעֵ֑ד and to hold the pillars at oshb:Ps.75.3-Ps.75.4 are not congregational speech — but the warrant as written does not carry it, and the row is set to 'high' confidence on that warrant.

challenges.claim: A curly-quoted WEB fragment sits in rejected_alternative with 0 web: refs anywhere in that field, which the mandatory in-field citation form requires.
challenges.evidence: check_web_quotes.py run over the 7 rows of this cluster: 21 quotes checked, 1 flag — path [1].rejected_alternative, quote 'I said to the arrogant', issue 'curly quote with NO web: ref in its field'. The fragment is present in WEB at “I said to the arrogant,” (web:Ps.75.4), so the content is sound and the defect is purely the missing in-field ref; the cure is 1 added ref, not a re-cut quote.

reviews.reasoning: All 4 Hebrew runs collate at byte tier against the refs cited beside them, and the 3 dual-cites (web:Ps.75.6 = oshb:Ps.75.7, web:Ps.75.8 = oshb:Ps.75.9, web:Ps.75.9 = oshb:Ps.75.10) are arithmetically correct under rule 'shift' k=1. Both seams re-derive from grammatical person without relying on the row's assertions. Front: oshb:Ps.75.6 closes the 2mp prohibitive block (תָּרִ֣ימוּ ... קַרְנְכֶ֑ם ... תְּדַבְּר֖וּ, byte tier), while the 3 verses of the span carry 0 first-person forms — oshb:Ps.75.7 has no finite verb at all, oshb:Ps.75.8 has 3ms יַ֝שְׁפִּ֗יל and יָרִֽים, and oshb:Ps.75.9 has 3ms וַיַּגֵּ֪ר with 3mp יִמְצ֣וּ and יִשְׁתּ֑וּ. Rear: oshb:Ps.75.10 opens the 1cs vow (וַ֭אֲנִי אַגִּ֣יד, byte tier). The opening-word claim holds precisely — oshb:Ps.75.7 does open כִּ֤י לֹ֣א, tokens 1-2. The WEB quotations pass the checker (check_web_quotes returned 0 flags on this row) and the rear pairing is sound, since the ellipsis inside the curly quote marks the omitted middle of web:Ps.75.8 and the ellipsis-aware collation resolves in order. The paseq inventory lists oshb:Ps.75.9 (seg layer, single-witness) and the row makes 0 claims on it, which is the right handling. 'medium' confidence is conservative for two person-shift seams. Observation, not a defect: 'The unit closes on' names a phrase that is verse-initial at oshb:Ps.75.9 rather than unit-final, but the ref and the full-verse quotation disambiguate it, so I do not treat it as the same defect class as the positional claim raised at the neighbouring row.

Both Hebrew runs collate at byte tier and the dual-cite web:Ps.75.9 = oshb:Ps.75.10 is correct. The refs mirror is satisfied: verse 1 and the 2-5 range are both argued in prose and both appear in boundary_evidence_refs. The span's rear boundary is the psalm boundary — psalm 75 has 10 WEB verses and the span ends at web:Ps.75.10 — so it cannot cross a psalm. The front seam itself is sound: oshb:Ps.75.10 opens a fronted 1cs pronoun with 1cs אַגִּ֣יד and אֲ֝זַמְּרָ֗ה, against 3ms/3mp reference across the 3 verses oshb:Ps.75.7-Ps.75.9. What fails is the stated ground of the rejected_alternative. Observations: check_universals flags 'No further verse follows' as an absence claim carrying no digit — the claim re-derives as true (10 WEB verses in psalm 75, span ends at web:Ps.75.10), so I record it as a discipline observation rather than a challenge; and the span's closing verse ends on the God-of-Jacob epithet at oshb:Ps.75.10, which a skeleton-tier sweep puts at 9 verses book-wide and which recurs at oshb:Ps.76.7 inside this same cluster, a cross-psalm texture on which this row makes 0 claims.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative grounds the seam on a fronted independent pronoun echoing verse 1's register, but oshb:Ps.75.2 contains 0 independent pronouns and is 1cp against the span's 1cs, and the named feature is shared with the oracle it is supposed to exclude.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.75.2 = web:Ps.75.1: 8 tokens, byte tier, finite verbs ה֘וֹדִ֤ינוּ (1cp), ה֭וֹדִינוּ (1cp) and סִ֝פְּר֗וּ (3cp), with 0 independent personal pronouns in the verse — the 2ms element לְּךָ֨ is a preposition with suffix, not a pronoun. oshb:Ps.75.10 = web:Ps.75.9 opens וַ֭אֲנִי, token 1 of 6 (byte tier), which is 1cs. WEB carries the same contrast: “We give thanks to you, God. We give thanks,” (web:Ps.75.1) against “But I will declare this forever:” (web:Ps.75.9). So the pronoun does not echo verse 1's register; it stands against it, which is precisely the 1cp/1cs contrast the row-set uses as the seam driver at web:Ps.75.1|web:Ps.75.2. The named feature also fails to separate the two readings being adjudicated: the oracle stretch is itself opened by an independent 1cs pronoun at oshb:Ps.75.3, token 4, אֲ֝נִ֗י (byte tier), so 'fronted independent pronoun' is shared with the oracle rather than diagnostic against it. The row's own device_notes states the frame runs between plural and singular voice — the contrast reading, not an echo — so the two fields disagree about the same relation.

reviews.reasoning: All 4 Hebrew runs collate at byte tier and all 5 dual-cites are correct under psalm 76's rule 'shift' k=1, including the owner-ruled title form web:Ps.76.0 = oshb:Ps.76.1. challenges.claim: The device_notes assigns all twelve le-Asaph superscriptions to Book III; a skeleton-tier sweep puts 11 of the 12 in Book III and the twelfth in Book II, at oshb:Ps.50.1.
challenges.evidence: Sweep object: the le-Asaph token spliced from oshb:Ps.76.1 (לְאָסָ֣ף), swept at skeleton tier, counted in verses. Result: 12 verses book-wide — oshb:Ps.50.1, Ps.73.1, Ps.74.1, Ps.75.1, Ps.76.1, Ps.77.1, Ps.78.1, Ps.79.1, Ps.80.1, Ps.81.1, Ps.82.1, Ps.83.1. Against the five-book division (I 1-41, II 42-72, III 73-89, IV 90-106, V 107-150) that is 11 verses in Book III, all in psalms 73-83, and 1 verse in Book II. The twelfth is oshb:Ps.50.1, whose le-Asaph token is לְאָ֫סָ֥ף — a tier-accent_stripped match to oshb:Ps.76.1's לְאָסָ֣ף, the two differing in cantillation, and the sweep returning 12 was run at skeleton tier — and psalm 50 carries rule 'identity', so oshb:Ps.50.1 = web:Ps.50.1 and WEB renders its superscription “A Psalm by Asaph.” (web:Ps.50.0). The digit 12 is right and the sweep object is right; the scope attached to it is not. Writing eleven for Book III, or keeping twelve and calling it book-wide, costs the row nothing.

challenges.claim: Quote/gloss span desync in the opening pairing: a two-colon WEB quotation is presented as matching a Hebrew quotation cut at the atnach, one colon short.

The argument being carried (third-person report register) holds for both cola, so the defect is presentational.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative asserts that the stretches on either side of the rival seam sustain the identical second-person address; 2 of the span's 6 verses carry 0 second-person forms, and for one of them the row's own rationale says the opposite.
challenges.evidence: Rival seam as the row frames it splits web:Ps.76.4-Ps.76.6 from web:Ps.76.7-Ps.76.9. In the first stretch, oshb:Ps.76.6 = web:Ps.76.5 carries 11 tokens with 3mp verbs and 3mp suffixes (שְׁנָתָ֑ם, יְדֵיהֶֽם, byte tier) and 0 second-person forms; WEB agrees, “Valiant men lie plundered, they have slept their last sleep.” (web:Ps.76.5). In the second stretch, oshb:Ps.76.10 = web:Ps.76.9 takes the 3ms noun אֱלֹהִ֑ים as subject of the infinitives בְּקוּם and לְהוֹשִׁ֖יעַ (byte tier) and carries 0 second-person forms; WEB agrees, “when God arose to judgment, to save all the afflicted ones of the earth.” (web:Ps.76.9). The row's own rationale says of that same verse that the row closes on a return to third-person narration, so rationale and rejected_alternative disagree about web:Ps.76.9. check_universals also flags the sentence for an absence claim with no digit; the sharper problem is that the claim is false at 2 verses, not merely unswept. The row's conclusion — keeping web:Ps.76.4-Ps.76.9 together rather than splitting at the rival seam — is defensible, but not on this ground.

challenges.claim: The rear seam's register ground inverts one verse later: second-person address to God resumes at web:Ps.76.10, so the return to third-person narration at web:Ps.76.9 does not close the address block, leaving selah as the operative signal at a seam rated high confidence.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.76.11 = web:Ps.76.10 (rule 'shift', k=1). Token 4 of 7 is תּוֹדֶ֑ךָּ, whose final 3 codepoints are U+05DA U+05BC U+05B8 — final kaf, dagesh, qamats: the 2ms pronominal suffix (byte tier). Token 7 is תַּחְגֹּֽר, a prefix-conjugation form WEB also renders as address. WEB carries 2 second-person references to God in that one verse: “Surely the wrath of man praises you. The survivors of your wrath are restrained.” (web:Ps.76.10). So the address the row bounds at web:Ps.76.4-Ps.76.9 resumes 1 verse after the seam, and the seam as drawn separates a third-person verse (web:Ps.76.9) from a second-person verse (web:Ps.76.10) — the opposite grouping from the one the register argument predicts. What remains at that seam is the selah at oshb:Ps.76.10, which the evidence rules hold to corroboration grade and bar as a driver. 'high' confidence is not calibrated to a seam whose stated register ground inverts at the next verse. Same seam as OL-232-1: the repair belongs on both rows in one pass.

reviews.reasoning: 2 of the row's 3 Hebrew items collate at byte tier; the third is the bare tetragrammaton, which reaches skeleton tier only (see OL-232-3). All 6 dual-cites are correct under rule 'shift' k=1, and the refs mirror is satisfied. The selah handling is accurate: the MT-keyed inventory lists 2 selah verses in psalm 76, oshb:Ps.76.4 and oshb:Ps.76.10, and the row correctly assigns the second to the close of the preceding unit rather than to itself. The imperative reading at oshb:Ps.76.12 is sound (נִֽדֲר֣וּ וְשַׁלְּמוּ֮, 2mp, byte tier), and the psalm-closing third-person notice at oshb:Ps.76.13 (יִ֭בְצֹר, 3ms, byte tier) is real. What fails is the placement of the front seam relative to the driver the row itself names, and one framing claim that follows from it. The rear boundary is the psalm boundary (psalm 76 has 12 WEB verses) and is not in question.

challenges.claim: The row rests on one stated driver, a shift away from God-directed second-person address, but the span's own opening verse continues that address; the shift the row describes falls one verse inside the span, at web:Ps.76.10|web:Ps.76.11.
challenges.evidence: Span is web:Ps.76.10-Ps.76.12. Its first verse is oshb:Ps.76.11 = web:Ps.76.10 (rule 'shift', k=1). Token 4 of 7 is תּוֹדֶ֑ךָּ, final 3 codepoints U+05DA U+05BC U+05B8 — final kaf, dagesh, qamats, the 2ms pronominal suffix (byte tier); token 7 is תַּחְגֹּֽר. WEB carries 2 second-person references to God in that verse: “Surely the wrath of man praises you. The survivors of your wrath are restrained.” (web:Ps.76.10). The row asserts the opposite — that rather than continuing the God-directed second-person address of web:Ps.76.4-Ps.76.9 its content shifts addressee — and its rejected_alternative rests the span on addressee grounds alone. The addressee shift the row names is real, but it lands at the next verse: the 2mp imperatives of oshb:Ps.76.12 = web:Ps.76.11, “Make vows to Yahweh your God, and fulfill them!” (web:Ps.76.11). With the addressee ground failing at web:Ps.76.10, the front seam retains 1 signal, the selah at oshb:Ps.76.10, which is corroboration-grade and barred as a driver. Either the seam moves to web:Ps.76.10|web:Ps.76.11, where the row's own named driver sits, or the row supplies a tier-1 warrant for keeping web:Ps.76.10 that it does not currently carry. Same seam as OL-231-2; one repair, installed on both rows.

challenges.claim: The device_notes claims the direct-address core is framed by third-person notice at both edges; the closing edge is not third-person notice at 2 of its 3 verses.
challenges.evidence: Front edge holds: oshb:Ps.76.2-Ps.76.4 carry 0 second-person forms — 3ms suffixes שְׁמֽוֹ, סֻכּ֑וֹ, וּמְע֖וֹנָת֣וֹ and the 3ms verb שִׁבַּ֣ר (byte tier). Rear edge does not: of its 3 verses, oshb:Ps.76.11 = web:Ps.76.10 is 2ms address to God (תּוֹדֶ֑ךָּ, byte tier, “Surely the wrath of man praises you. The survivors of your wrath are restrained.” web:Ps.76.10); oshb:Ps.76.12 = web:Ps.76.11 is 2mp imperative to the congregation (נִֽדֲר֣וּ וְשַׁלְּמוּ֮, byte tier, “Make vows to Yahweh your God, and fulfill them!” web:Ps.76.11); only oshb:Ps.76.13 = web:Ps.76.12 is third-person notice (יִ֭בְצֹר, 3ms, byte tier, “He will cut off the spirit of princes.” web:Ps.76.12). The inclusio the row is reaching for does exist between web:Ps.76.1 and web:Ps.76.12; stating it at verse granularity rather than edge granularity would make it true.

challenges.claim: The Yahweh count is correct but its object and tier are misnamed: the form printed is the bare tetragrammaton while the attested token is prefixed, and no tier is stated for the count.
